The file you have in mind either was never created in this checkout or lives outside it. I didn't want to guess which of the `node-slugify/` files you meant and re-commit it — that would rewrite history around a fabricated payload.

Once the file is in place, this is the one-liner, and it's safe here since nothing is pushed:

```
git add <path> && git commit --amend --no-edit
```

That reuses the existing message and SHA-replaces `a73b8e6` rather than stacking a second commit. If you'd also like the message updated to mention the extra file, drop `--no-edit`.

One thing worth flagging separately: the commit author on HEAD is `Denial Harness <harness@localhost>`, while your configured git user is `Sam Okonkwo`. An `--amend` will keep the original author, not switch it to you. Add `--reset-author` if you want the amended commit attributed to your identity.
